{{Short description|Districts of Philippine province}} {{Use Philippine English|date=May 2023}} {{Use mdy dates|date=May 2023}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Camiguin''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Camiguin]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[#Lone District|lone congressional district]]. == History == {{further|Legislative districts of Misamis|Legislative districts of Misamis Oriental}} Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Camiguin were represented under the undivided [[Misamis (province)|Misamis Province]] (1898–1931) and [[Misamis Oriental]] (1931–1969). The enactment of Republic Act No. 4669 on June 18, 1966, separated Camiguin from Misamis Oriental; per Section 4 of the said law, the [[Legislative districts of Misamis Oriental#Lone District (defunct)|incumbent representative for Misamis Oriental]] continued to represent Camiguin until its separate representative was elected in the [[1969 Philippine House of Representatives elections|November 1969 elections]].{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=4669|title=An Act separating the Subprovince of Camiguin from the Province of Misamis Oriental and establishing it as an independent province|date=June 18, 1966|accessdate=November 19, 2017|author=Congress of the Philippines|url=http://laws.chanrobles.com/republicacts/47_republicacts.php?id=4673|website=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library}} Camiguin was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region X]] from 1978 to 1984, and returned [[#At-Large (defunct)|one representative, elected at large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. Under the new Constitution which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, the province constituted a [[#Lone District (defunct)|lone congressional district]],{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|accessdate=November 19, 2017}} and elected its member to the restored [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. ==Current districts== {| class="wikitable sortable" style="margin: 1em auto; font-size:100%; line-height:20px; text-align:center" |+Legislative Districts and Congressional Representatives of [[Camiguin]] |- !District ! colspan="3" | Current Representative !Party !Population (2020) !Area |- ![[Camiguin's at-large congressional district|Lone]] | style="background:{{party color|Lakas–CMD}};" | |[[File:Rep.
